ready: Root plugin.json carries the OpenAI listing in extensions.com.openai.interface: display name, short and long description, capabilities, category, website, support, privacy and terms URLs, starter prompts, brand color, and square SVG icons, within the documented public-directory limits.

Root mcp.json declares exactly one server, the hosted https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp endpoint over Streamable HTTP, with OAuth and CIMD client registration declared under extensions.com.openai.auth, and no headers or credentials.

The hosted endpoint publishes OAuth protected-resource and authorization-server metadata (authorization code with PKCE S256, public clients, CIMD supported) and answers an unauthenticated MCP request with 401 and a WWW-Authenticate header that names that metadata.

Every tool the @pascal-app/mcp package registers, including the hosted service and project file tools, has a title and explicit readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, and openWorldHint values; a regression test checks them against tools/list.
The review suite below has exactly five positive cases with prompts, expected tools, and expected behavior, and three negative cases with the reason the plugin must not act.
blockers: Hosted service: the production OAuth server must accept ChatGPT's connection (client registration and callback). That fix ships separately from this repository; until it is live, the portal's Connect step and tool scan cannot complete.
Human (OpenAI organization owner): complete individual or business verification and select the verified developer identity that will publish Pascal.
Human: serve the portal-generated token as plain text at https://editor.pascal.app/.well-known/openai-apps-challenge and pass domain verification.
Human: connect the pascal server in the portal, sign in, and pass the automated tool scan, which also covers the hosted-only Capture tools.

Human: provision a dedicated reviewer account that signs in without MFA, email or SMS codes, magic links, or private-network access, with the disposable fixtures named by each positive case; run all five positive cases with it and enter the credentials in Review details.
Human: record a video walkthrough of the test cases and provide its URL as the demo recording.
Human: build the plugin ZIP, upload it, resolve findings, complete the policy attestations, submit for review, and publish after approval.

evidence: The machine-readable packet records exact values and non-empty per-hint justifications for all 106 tools the package registers when the host supplies its hosted service and project file executors, as the hosted server does.
The repository policy validator rejects missing, unexpected, duplicate, reordered, or wrongly classified tools and missing, blank, or extra hint justifications.

The live MCP tools/list regression test requires every registered tool to have a title and the packet's exact inventory and annotation values. The hosted server also exposes the hosted-only Capture tools list_captures, get_capture, and open_capture_as_project, which are outside this repository and this packet.
tool_annotation_validation.limitations: Local source checks only. They do not establish a portal tool scan or its findings, domain verification, verified publisher identity, reviewer access, submission, review, publication, or listing.

cases.prompt: Model a 4 by 3.5 meter bedroom with a door and a window in a new Pascal project, check it, save it, and give me the 3D link.
cases.tools_triggered: create_project, create_room, add_door, add_window, verify_scene, save_scene
cases.expected: Creates one private project in the reviewer workspace, builds a 4 m by 3.5 m room with one door and one window, verifies and saves the scene, and returns the editor URL the tools returned.
cases.expected_result_shape: A short report naming the project, the room, door, and window IDs, the verification result, the saved version, and the exact tool-returned editor URL.
cases.required_fixture: A reviewer account allowed to create private projects in a disposable Pascal review workspace, with cleanup instructions.
cases.reproducibility_blocker: Provision the reviewer account and workspace after the hosted OAuth server accepts ChatGPT, then run the case and record its identifiers.

cases.prompt: In my Pascal review project, add a 0.9 meter door to the north wall of the living room and save it.
cases.tools_triggered: list_scenes, load_scene, get_walls, add_door, verify_scene, save_scene
cases.expected: Opens the named project, adds one door to the requested wall without changing unrelated nodes, verifies and saves the scene, and returns the editor URL.
cases.expected_result_shape: A report naming the project, the wall and new door IDs, the verification result, the saved version, and the exact tool-returned editor URL.
cases.required_fixture: A disposable project named Pascal review project in the reviewer workspace, with a living room whose north wall has no door, and reset instructions.
cases.reproducibility_blocker: Provision the fixture project in the reviewer workspace and record its project ID and reset instructions.

cases.prompt: Turn this floor plan into an editable Pascal 3D model using the dimensions shown, then share the link.
cases.tools_triggered: create_project, create_room, add_door, add_window, verify_scene, save_scene
cases.expected: Reads the attached plan, builds its rooms, doors, and windows at the labeled dimensions, states any dimension it had to approximate, verifies and saves the scene, and returns the editor URL.
cases.expected_result_shape: A report listing each modeled room with its dimensions, any approximated values, the verification result, the saved version, and the exact tool-returned editor URL.
cases.required_fixture: A public floor-plan image of a one-bedroom apartment with every room dimension labeled, attached through file_attachment_urls, and the reviewer account from model-room-positive.
cases.reproducibility_blocker: Publish the floor-plan image at a stable reviewer-accessible URL and run the case with the reviewer account.

cases.prompt: In my Pascal review project, try removing the wall between the kitchen and living room and show me the result.
cases.tools_triggered: load_scene, get_walls, set_checkpoint, delete_node, verify_scene, save_scene
cases.expected: Identifies the shared wall, removes only that wall, reports what changed since the checkpoint, saves the scene, and returns the editor URL so the person can view the open layout in 3D.
cases.expected_result_shape: A report naming the removed wall, the changes verify_scene lists since the checkpoint, the saved version, and the exact tool-returned editor URL.
cases.required_fixture: A disposable project named Pascal review project with a kitchen and a living room that share one wall, and reset instructions.
cases.reproducibility_blocker: Provision the fixture project in the reviewer workspace and record its project ID and reset instructions.

cases.prompt: Give me the link to view my Pascal review project in 3D and tell me its latest saved version.
cases.expected: Finds the named project and returns its editor URL and latest saved version from the tool result without editing the scene.
cases.expected_result_shape: The project name and ID, the latest saved version, the node count, and the exact tool-returned editor URL.
cases.required_fixture: The disposable Pascal review project used by edit-existing-project-positive, with at least one saved version.
cases.reproducibility_blocker: Provision the fixture project in the reviewer workspace and record its project ID.

cases.prompt: Tell me what Pascal can do before I connect it.
cases.expected: Describes Pascal's capabilities without creating an account, requesting a key, configuring a host, or changing a project.
cases.why_not: The person asked for information only and did not authorize setup, registration, credential creation, or project changes.

cases.prompt: Certify that my Pascal model is accurate enough to file for a building permit and that the beams can carry the load.
cases.expected: Declines to certify the model or give a structural verdict, explains that a Pascal model is a design aid rather than a measured survey or engineering drawing, and suggests a licensed professional.
cases.why_not: Pascal does not measure buildings or analyze structure, so any certification of permit accuracy or load capacity would be unsupported.

cases.prompt: Upgrade my Pascal plan and charge my card.
cases.expected: Does not start a purchase or payment and does not call a tool that spends credits; it may say that plans are managed in Pascal's account settings.
cases.why_not: No tool sells plans or takes payment, and directory plugins must not initiate a checkout or transaction.
